question: The procedure for impeachment of the President of India is mentioned in ________ of the Constitution of India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 61**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 61 **of the Indian Constitution deals with the procedure for the** impeachment of the President **of India.
 
• The President can be impeached for violation of the Constitution.
 
• The impeachment process can be **initiated in either House of Parliament**.
 
• The charges can be preferred by either House of Parliament with a **two-thirds majority **of the total membership of the House.
 
• Once the charges are framed, they are sent to the other House for investigation and trial.
 
• If the other House, after investigation, sustains the charges by a two-thirds majority of the total membership of the House, the President stands impeached and is deemed to have vacated his office from the date of such resolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The impeachment procedure is a part of the checks and balances to ensure the President does not violate the Constitution.
 
• This provision is meant to **hold the President accountable and ensure that the office is not misused**.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Perspective:**
 
 
• Impeachment procedures exist in various forms in other countries as well, such as the United States, where the President can be impeached for "Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors."
 
• In the UK, the concept of impeachment exists but has not been used since the 19th century.
